name: Single statement
idea: One enormous headline carries the whole section; everything else is small, quiet and precisely aligned beneath it.

name: Editorial split
idea: Two unequal columns like a magazine spread: a narrow column of labels and a wide column of content, with a strong vertical rule or margin between them.

name: Bento grid
idea: Content broken into tiles of clearly different sizes on one grid; the most important tile is at least twice the size of any other.

name: Comparison table
idea: The content laid out as a real table or matrix the eye can scan in rows and columns, with one row or column emphasised.

name: Narrative scroll
idea: A sequence of short full-width beats, one idea per screen, that reads top to bottom like a story with a clear ending and call to action.

name: Numbered steps
idea: Content reorganised as a numbered sequence (01, 02, 03) with large numerals as the main graphic device.

name: Sticky rail
idea: A side rail (title, summary or call to action) that stays in place while the detail scrolls past it. Falls back to a normal stack on phones.

name: Interactive switch
idea: One compact stage whose content changes with a toggle, tabs or a slider, so the visitor explores options instead of scrolling a list. Must work with the keyboard.

name: Proof first
idea: Lead with the strongest existing evidence (numbers, logos, quotes, results) at full scale; the explanation comes second and smaller.

name: Minimal list
idea: No cards and no boxes: a plain, beautifully spaced list with hairline dividers, where typography alone creates the hierarchy.

name: Asymmetric poster
idea: Deliberately off-centre composition with large empty space on one side and tightly packed content on the other, like a printed poster.

name: Spec sheet
idea: Content presented as a technical data sheet: label and value pairs, small caps or monospace labels, dense but perfectly aligned.

name: Media led
idea: The existing imagery or illustration is the hero at its natural shape; text is arranged around it and never on top of it.

name: Question led
idea: Organised around the questions a visitor actually has; each block opens with the question and answers it in one or two lines.

name: Stacked cards
idea: Large cards that overlap or stack as the page scrolls, one in focus at a time, each with one clear point.

name: Timeline
idea: Content placed along a visible horizontal or vertical line (before and after, now and next, or chronological order).

name: Dense dashboard
idea: High information density done well: many small, well-labelled modules visible at once, for a visitor who wants everything on one screen.

name: Centred and calm
idea: A narrow centred column with generous white space, one accent, and a single obvious next action. Nothing decorative.
